title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 401–403): Grothendieck builds an algebraic, group-scheme 'paraphrase' of the profinite objects attached to M_{0,3}, in his 'equation des lacets' setting.

- He has a group scheme M_{ρ,σ} over a base S. It is attached to a pair (ρ, σ) of elements of GL(2), ρ of order 6 and σ of order 4. These generalize the standard generators of SL(2,Z).
- M_{ρ,σ} has a normal subgroup 𝔊^+_{ρ,σ} = SG ≅ SL(2)_S, the analogue of Ĝ^+_{0,3}.
- The quotient is T^!_{ρ,σ}, essentially a torus-like group sitting in T_0 × T_ρ × N'_σ. So there is an extension 1 → 𝔊^+ → M → T^! → 1 (formula (30)).
- This extension has a canonical semidirect splitting through a subgroup M_{ρ,σ}(ω) (formula (31)).

This page:
- Formula (32) restates the splitting. A subgroup M^!_{ρ,σ}(o) ⊂ M_{ρ,σ} maps isomorphically onto T^!_{ρ,σ} under the canonical projection. It is the analogue of the subgroup M^{!~}_{0,3}(o) ⊂ M^~_{0,3} from an earlier section (§4?, V).

Remark (the main point of the page):
- In the profinite/discrete theory there is a finer structure. The group Ĝ^+ contains the fundamental group π of P^1−{0,1,∞} (≈ Γ(2), up to ±1) with quotient 𝔖_3, the automorphism group of {0,1,∞}.
- One would therefore like a group T_{ρ,σ} that is a (product) extension of T^! by 𝔖_3, together with a subgroup π_{ρ,σ} ⊂ 𝔊^+ with 𝔊^+/π ≅ 𝔖_3.
- Grothendieck observes this is impossible for group schemes, even in the modular case. The reason: 𝔊^+ ≅ SL(2)_S has connected fibres, so it has no nontrivial finite étale quotient. The profinite congruence structure is invisible algebraically.

Modular case (ρ = [[0,1],[−1,1]], σ = [[0,1],[−1,0]]):
- One can still introduce a canonical section τ = τ_∞ of T^!_{ρ,σ}, formula (33).
- Its representative in Γ(M^!_{ρ,σ}(o)) is τ_∞ = diag(−1, +1), formula (34). This matrix has determinant −1 and acts on the upper half plane by z ↦ −z̄. It is the 'complex conjugation' / anti-holomorphic involution.
- Check: τσ τ^{-1} = σ^{-1}. τρτ^{-1} = [[0,−1],[1,1]], which has trace 1, order 6 and is conjugate to ρ^{-1}. So τ_∞ is an orientation-reversing symmetry of the pair (ρ, σ) up to conjugation, as expected.

Next page: Grothendieck asks whether, outside the modular case, one can define 'anti-involutions' generalizing τ'_∞ = [[0,1],[1,0]], τ_1 = [[−1,1],[0,1]] and τ_∞. These three are the reflections in the sides of the (2,3,∞) fundamental triangle, generating PGL(2,Z), as in his §42, IV. He is 'convinced' the answer is yes.
errors: No mathematical error. The connectedness argument is correct: a homomorphism from a group scheme with connected fibres such as SL(2)_S to a finite étale group such as 𝔖_3 is trivial, so no subgroup π with quotient 𝔖_3 can exist.

Minor point: τ_∞ does not literally normalize ρ. It sends ρ to a conjugate of ρ^{-1}, so 'section' must be read in Grothendieck's group M_{ρ,σ} of symmetries up to conjugation, not as an element of the normalizer of ρ.

ideas.what: Algebraic group-scheme analogue M_{ρ,σ} ⊃ SL(2) of the profinite group M^~_{0,3} ⊃ Ĝ^+_{0,3}, with a split extension by a torus-like quotient T^!
ideas.modern_name: Algebraic hull / Zariski-closure analogue of SL2(Z)-type symmetry groups; motivic or pro-algebraic versions of Grothendieck–Teichmüller objects
ideas.usually_credited_to: Pro-unipotent / pro-algebraic GT: Drinfeld (1990), Deligne (1989), Ihara
ideas.where_published: Only in these 'Longue Marche' sequel notes (cote 140-3)

ideas.what: Observation that the 𝔖_3 = SL2(Z/2)-type quotient (Γ(2) ⊂ SL2(Z), fundamental group of P^1−{0,1,∞}) cannot be mirrored in the group-scheme context because SL(2) is connected
ideas.modern_name: Connected group schemes have no finite étale quotients; congruence subgroups are not algebraic

ideas.what: Canonical anti-involution τ_∞ = diag(−1,1) in the modular case, and the reflections generating PGL(2,Z)
ideas.modern_name: Extended modular group PGL2(Z) as a (2,3,∞) reflection group; complex conjugation acting on the tower
ideas.where_published: Possibly touched on in La Longue Marche (§42 is cited internally)

missed.claim: Grothendieck asks whether, for general (ρ, σ) and not only the modular pair, there are canonical 'anti-involutions' in the group-scheme M_{ρ,σ} generalizing the three reflections of PGL2(Z). He states he is convinced this holds but gives no construction on this page.
missed.quote: Il serait intéressant de voir si, en dehors des cas modulaire, on peut introduire des "antiinvolutions"
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a modest question about real structures on generalized 'lacets' group schemes. It is likely easy or answered implicitly, but it is not recorded as such in the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: These are internal bookkeeping for Grothendieck's unpublished group-scheme analogue of the M_{0,3} symmetries. The remarks themselves (no 𝔖_3 quotient of a connected group; diag(−1,1) as complex conjugation) are standard. Only the overall framework is unpublished.
transcription_corrections: The groups written 𝔖^+_{ρ,σ} in the remark should be 𝔊^+_{ρ,σ} (= SG ≅ SL(2), as defined on the previous page). Only 𝔖_3 is the symmetric group.
'M^!_{ρ,σ}(0)' is probably '(o)' or '(ω)', consistent with M_{ρ,σ}(ω) on the previous page.
The section reference '§48, V' is uncertain in the image; it could read '§45, V'.
The page number at the bottom left is 402 (archive page).
